In [[differential geometry]], a field in [[mathematics]], a '''multivector field''', '''polyvector field''' of '''degree ''<math>k</math>''''', or '''''<math>k</math>''-vector field''', on a [[Differentiable manifold|smooth manifold]] <math>M</math>, is a generalization of the notion of a [[vector field]] on a manifold. 

== Definition ==
A multivector field of degree ''<math>k</math>'' is a [[global section]] <math>X</math> of the ''k''th [[exterior power]] <math>\wedge^k TM \to M</math> of the [[tangent bundle]], i.e. <math>X</math> assigns to each point <math>p \in M</math> a [[Multivector|''<math>k</math>-''vector]] in <math>\wedge^k T_p M</math>. 

The set of all multivector fields of degree ''<math>k</math>'' on <math>M</math> is denoted by <math>\mathfrak{X}^k (M) := \Gamma (\wedge^k TM)</math> or by <math>T^k_{\rm poly}(M)</math>. 

=== Particular cases ===

* If ''<math>k=0</math>'' one has <math>\mathfrak{X}^0 (M) := \mathcal{C}^\infty(M)</math>;
* If ''<math>k=1</math>'', one has <math>\mathfrak{X}^1 (M) := \mathfrak{X}(M)</math>, i.e. one recovers the notion of vector field;
* If ''<math>k > \mathrm{dim} (M)</math>'', one has <math>\mathfrak{X}^k (M) := \{0\}</math>, since <math>\wedge^k TM = 0</math>.

== Algebraic structures ==
The set <math>\mathfrak{X}^k (M)</math> of multivector fields is an <math>\mathbb{R}</math>-vector space for every ''<math>k</math>'', so that <math>\mathfrak{X}^\bullet (M) = \bigoplus_k \mathfrak{X}^k (M)</math> is a [[graded vector space]].

Furthermore, there is a wedge product

<math display="block">\wedge: \mathfrak{X}^k (M) \times \mathfrak{X}^l (M) \to \mathfrak{X}^{k+l} (M)</math>

which for ''<math>k=0</math>'' and ''<math>l=1</math>'' recovers the standard action of smooth functions on vector fields. Such product is associative and graded commutative, making <math>(\mathfrak{X}^\bullet (M), \wedge)</math> into a [[Graded-commutative ring|graded commutative algebra]].

Similarly, the [[Lie bracket of vector fields]] extends to the so-called [[Schouten–Nijenhuis bracket|Schouten-Nijenhuis bracket]]

<math display="block">[\cdot,\cdot]: \mathfrak{X}^k (M) \times \mathfrak{X}^l (M) \to \mathfrak{X}^{k+l-1} (M)</math>

which is <math>\mathbb{R}</math>-bilinear, graded skew-symmetric and satisfies the graded version of the Jacobi identity. Furthermore, it satisfies a graded version of the Leibniz identity, i.e. it is compatible with the wedge product, making the triple <math>(\mathfrak{X}^\bullet (M), \wedge, [\cdot,\cdot])</math> into a [[Gerstenhaber algebra]].

== Comparison with differential forms ==
Since the tangent bundle is dual to the [[cotangent bundle]], multivector fields of degree ''<math>k</math>'' are dual to ''<math>k</math>''-[[differential forms|forms]], and both are subsumed in the general concept of a [[tensor field]], which is a section of some [[Tensor field#Tensor bundles|tensor bundle]], often consisting of exterior powers of the tangent and cotangent bundles. A <math>(k,0)</math>-tensor field is a differential <math>k</math>-form, a <math>(0,1)</math>-tensor field is a vector field, and a <math>(0,k)</math>-tensor field is <math>k</math>-vector field.

While differential forms are widely studied as such in [[differential geometry]] and [[differential topology]], multivector fields are often encountered as tensor fields of type <math>(0,k)</math>, except in the context of the [[geometric algebra]] (see also [[Clifford algebra]]).<ref>{{Cite book|title=Geometric algebra for physicists|last=Doran, Chris (Chris J. L.)|date=2007|publisher=Cambridge University Press|others=Lasenby, A. N. (Anthony N.), 1954-|isbn=9780521715959|edition=1st pbk. ed. with corr|location=Cambridge|oclc=213362465}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|title=Geometric algebra|last=Artin, Emil, 1898-1962.|year=1988|orig-date=1957|publisher=Interscience Publishers|isbn=9781118164518|location=New York|oclc=757486966}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|title=A new approach to differential geometry using Clifford's geometric algebra|last=Snygg, John.|date=2012|publisher=Springer Science+Business Media, LLC|isbn=9780817682835|location=New York|oclc=769755408}}</ref>
